blurb: Fields of fractions, p-adic valuations, periodic expansions, Farey sequences, continued fractions and approximation.

pics.alt: Ford circles drawn above the fractions 0, 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, 2/5, 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 3/4, 4/5 and 1 on the number line
pics.caption: Ford circles: above each reduced fraction p/q sits a circle of radius 1/(2q²). Two circles touch exactly when their fractions are Farey neighbours, and otherwise they are disjoint.
pics.title: Ford circles.svg

pics.alt: A section of the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus with hieratic text and triangle diagrams
pics.caption: A section of the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus (British Museum, EA 10057), copied by the scribe Ahmes around 1550 BC. The papyrus opens with a table writing 2/n as a sum of unit fractions and does all its arithmetic in Egyptian fractions.
pics.title: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus.jpg
